Chinese media have reacted with glee to the dramatic reinstatement of Jensen Huang as the chief executive of Nvidia, with one commentary warning against future “witch-hunts”.

title: Chinese media hail Huang’s Nvidia return with warning over ‘witch-hunts’

author: Edward Helmore
description:
New York City mayor notes ‘massive impact’ on working Americans’ lives when Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, on Monday weighed in on the corporate turbulence surrounding Nvidia and the chipmaker’s chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, saying he does not think working Americans “signed up for their pensions being tied to the question of … Huang’s fidelity to his marriage”.

The mayor said Huang “had a massive impact”, with Nvidia’s share price dropping dramatically when Huang stepped down as the company’s CEO on 12 November after a reported extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
title: Mamdani says Nvidia drama shows stock market is overly dependent on AI

author: Wing Kuang
description:
Several members of the group chat set up after the alleged murder of Feng Jianming say they or their parents were called by police from their home towns in China

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Chinese police have contacted several people who were part of a WeChat group that discussed attending a Melbourne vigil for Feng Jianming, the HungryPanda food delivery rider allegedly murdered earlier this month.

At least three members of the group set up after Feng’s death said they were contacted, raising concerns that Chinese authorities may have been alerted to discussions about the protest activity either automatically or manually by the Chinese-owned messaging and social app.
title: Chinese police contacted members of WeChat group after they discussed Melbourne vigil for HungryPanda rider

author: Josh Butler
description:
Australians also turn against AI datacentres, with nearly half saying they don’t want one near their home

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese’s approval ratings have nosedived in the latest Guardian Essential poll, with the prime minister reaching his highest level of disapproval after his net popularity plummeted 10 points in just a month.

Australians have also turned strongly against AI datacentres, with nearly half of the country saying they don’t want one near their home. Women, older people and One Nation and Greens supporters are among the most likely to reject living near a datacentre.
title: Guardian Essential poll: Albanese’s disapproval rating hits highest level as problems mount for Labor

description:

Days out from the Victorian state election, the fate of nine datacentre projects remains uncertain, with some companies confident they will be able to get their projects across the line after Saturday.

title: Days out from the Victorian election, nine datacentre projects await approval. What will their fate be?

author: Kiran Stacey and Patrick Butler
description:
Benefit claims made easier in first stage of shake-up of welfare system

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Disabled people with severe and lifelong conditions will be able to claim disability benefits more easily after a major review of the system by ministers.

The Department for Work and Pensions said on Tuesday it would immediately commit to speeding up the personal independence payment (Pip) system for adults in England and Wales who have severe conditions or ones that are unlikely to change.

Continue reading...
title: Ministers approve fast-track disability payments in England and Wales

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
World’s largest catering group supplies big tech firms such as Microsoft, Google and Amazon in the US

  • Business live – latest updates

London’s stock market has been dealt a further blow as the catering company Compass Group confirmed plans to move its main listing to the US, saying it had become “a predominantly North American business”.

The world’s largest catering group said the move would provide better access to “the world’s largest and deepest pool of capital,” as it kicked off a consultation with its shareholders, two-fifths of whom are based in the US.
title: NHS caterer Compass confirms plan to ditch main London listing for New York

Huang, who was forced to step down briefly over allegations of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected spy, returned to the company’s HQ in Santa Clara, California, receiving a hero’s welcome.

author: Lois Beckett
description:
Seasonal high tides and rising ocean levels can disrupt flights and flood roads, with the San Francisco Bay Area facing some of the greatest risks

Starting this morning, seasonal high tides up and down the coast of California are expected to drive “major to extreme” coastal flooding, with the San Francisco Bay Area currently seen as being at the highest risk of travel-related flooding delays.

The first of the year’s highest “king tides” will arrive in much of southern California, including parts of San Diego and Los Angeles, before 9am on Tuesday, and in the Bay Area between 10 and 11am, according to tidal estimates from the California Coastal Commission.

Continue reading...
title: California king tides threaten Thanksgiving travel as coastal flooding looms

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
Juliana Stratton eager to work with Republicans who ‘have a real spine’ to stand up to Trump and deliver for voters

Juliana Stratton, the incoming Democratic senator from Illinois, said she would support significantly reforming or abolishing the filibuster in order to allow Congress to deliver on the promises they made American voters.

The filibuster means that most successful legislation in the Senate must have 60 supporters instead of a simple majority. Eliminating that requirement is one of several reforms Democrats can act on after they won an unexpected 56-44 majority in the next US Senate, their largest majority in nearly two decades.

Continue reading...
title: History-making Democratic senator backs filibuster reform to make good on midterm pledges

author: Donna Lu Assistant editor, climate, environment and science
description:
Georgina Long and subatomic physicist Anthony Thomas recognised in Prime Minister’s Prizes for Science

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

When Prof Georgina Long was starting out in melanoma treatment and research, “my waiting room would change so rapidly”.

Referring to her patients with stage 4 melanoma, the oncologist and medical director at the Melanoma Institute Australia said she wouldn’t “see the same face for more than nine months, 12 months maximum”.

Continue reading...
title: Researcher who helped improve melanoma survival rates among winners of top Australian science prize

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Total number of drivers dropped 5% over the last year and fell 15% compared with 2019 levels, new report finds

The number of school bus drivers in the US has dropped 5% over the last year as drivers continue to experience low pay, poor working conditions and school budget shortfalls, according to a new report.

The total number of school bus drivers is down 15%, or nearly 34,000 drivers, compared with 2019 levels, according to an new analysis from the Economic Policy Institute.

Continue reading...
title: US school bus drivers decline amid low pay and poor work conditions

author: Shrai Popat
description:
Lawmakers from both parties are demanding answers about the Nvidia CEO’s reinstatement and the administration’s handling of national security risks

Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s chief executive is “exhibit A” of the “political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration’s big tech and AI policy”, Chris Van Hollen, the Maryland Democrat vying to become the next Senate majority leader, told reporters Monday.

Van Hollen said he intends to focus on Huang’s “efforts to increase and accelerate the export of high-end chips to China, how he’s been accomplishing that, how he’s been getting his way with the administration” when the reinstalled Nvidia CEO appears before the Senate banking committee on 3 December.

Continue reading...
title: Congress to grill Jensen Huang over ties with China and Trump’s intervention

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Wanda Dench texted stranger Jamal Hinton by mistake in 2016 – and pair have shared holiday together ever since

The heartwarming story of the Arizona grandmother and the stranger to whom she inadvertently texted a Thanksgiving invitation in 2016 – leading to their sharing the holiday together annually ever since – is getting the Lifetime movie treatment, according to the principals of the tale.

Jamal Hinton announced recently that he, Wanda Dench and their Thanksgiving tradition were taking “the next step” with the cable television channel known for its sentimental films, especially those themed around the festive season.
title: Tale of Thanksgiving grandma and accidental guest to receive Lifetime movie treatment

title: Timms says Pip review being published today will ‘rehumanise’ benefit – UK politics live

Meanwhile, Hungary’s prime minister Péter Magyar announced a visit to the border region of Transcarpathia for talks with Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Announcing the visit on Facebook, Magyar said:

“Together with [foreign] minister Anita Orbán, we will visit several Hungarian institutions. This is the first visit by a Hungarian prime minister to Ukraine since 2015.”

Continue reading...

“It is foreseeable that the malicious attempts to sow discord in China-US relations will not automatically disappear simply because Huang has been reinstated.”

Amendments to government bill by Coalition and Greens would establish protections for those reporting wrongdoing in sport

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Whistleblowers coming forward to report corruption or misconduct in sports would be protected under draft laws put forward by the Coalition and the Greens, in response to the fallout of the Australian cricket ball tampering scandal.

The South Africa tour of 2018 is back in the national spotlight after the release of Usman Khawaja’s autobiography earlier this month, in which he claimed players had used sandpaper to tamper with the ball be
title: Sports whistleblowers protected under proposed laws amid Australian cricket ball tampering saga

author: Robert Mackey
description:
Singapore-based company entangled in scandal over alleged spy Alice Huang’s affair with Jensen Huang

The US commerce department published an official notice on Monday adding the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and its subsidiaries in Thailand and Malaysia, to a trade blacklist.

Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner which has been under investigation by US authorities since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, will now need approval from the commerce department to obtain US exports, which is likely to be denied.

Continue reading...
title: US adds Megaspeed, AI firm at center of Nvidia scandal, to trade blacklist

author: Kat Wong
description:
Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Baird’s Paddington home in February 2024

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon could have sat in silence and let the crown “do its worst”, but he made the choice to take the “long walk” to the witness box, a jury has been told.

Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.

title: Beau Lamarre-Condon chose ‘long walk’ to witness box rather than silence, his barrister tells court
